We need to propose a retrosynthesis route with at least 5 reactions, using templates in order: ['29646', '1914389', '1914390', '149040', '1914391'].

We have applied first three templates, but need to continue with 149040 and 1914391. Also need to construct JSON route with molecules and reactions.

We need to get precursors for each step using apply_template. For each template, we need to apply to current molecule to get precursors. We have for template 29646 applied to target gave three possible precursors (list). We need to choose one that can be further processed by next template 1914389. The earlier attempts show that one of the precursors is "C/C(=C/[C@H]1O[C@@H](C/C=C/C=C/C(=O)O)C[C@H](O)[C@H]1C)CO" (without silyl). That matches template 1914389 (True). So we can choose that as intermediate.

Now apply 1914389 to that intermediate gave two precursors: "C/C(=C/[C@H]1O[C@@H](CC=O)C[C@H](O)[C@H]1C)CO" and "CCOC(=O)/C=C/CP(=O)(OCC)OCC". So after second reaction we have two branches? Typically retrosynthesis splits into two precursors. So we need to continue each branch with remaining templates in order? The order list is fixed: after 1914389, we must apply 1914390, then 149040, then 1914391. Likely each step applies to each precursor individually? Might be sequential chain: each reaction transforms a molecule to precursors, then each precursor may be further transformed by next template. But we have two precursors; we need to apply next template to each? The order list maybe for the whole route, meaning first reaction uses 29646, second uses 1914389, third uses 1914390, fourth uses 149040, fifth uses 1914391. So we need a linear chain of 5 reactions, not branching. So we need to select a single precursor at each step that can be further transformed by next template.

Thus after 1914389 we have two possible precursors; we need to pick one that matches template 1914390. We checked that "C/C(=C/[C@H]1O[C@@H](CC=O)C[C@H](O)[C@H]1C)CO" matches 1914390 (True). The other "CCOC(=O)/C=C/CP(=O)(OCC)OCC" maybe also matches? Not sure. But we can continue with the first.

Now apply template 1914390 to that molecule. We attempted earlier and got empty result. Actually earlier we applied 1914390 to that molecule and got empty result. That suggests maybe the template expects a different orientation (maybe forward vs retro).
